body:
Found while working the #260 direction from the MIM side. MediaIngredientMech needs records for the 44 CultureMech ingredient names it lacks, so I verified CultureMech's `term.id` for each before adopting it. **They should not be adopted as-is.**

## 1. One grounding names an unrelated compound

    Sodium sulfide  ->  CHEBI:85357

`CHEBI:85357` is **`3-[(1E,4R)-4-hydroxycyclohex-2-en-1-ylidene]pyruvic acid`**, formula `C9H10O4` — an organic acid. Sodium sulfide is `Na2S`:

    CHEBI:76208  sodium sulfide (anhydrous)   2Na.S
    CHEBI:76209  sodium sulfide nonahydrate   9H2O.2Na.S

This is the same shape as the `Cysteine-HCl` → `CHEBI:52891` (a fluorescent quencher dye) error I flagged on #272. Two independent instances suggests a systematic cause rather than two typos — worth finding whatever produced both.

**The cheap detector**: compare the ChEBI *label* of each assigned id against the ingredient name and flag any pair sharing no token. It is how `KF` → `Lys-Phe` was caught in MIM.

## 2. Stereochemistry silently dropped

    DL-Tyrosine    ->  CHEBI:17895  L-tyrosine
    DL-threonine   ->  CHEBI:16857  L-threonine

A racemate is not its L-enantiomer. `CHEBI:18186 tyrosine` is stereo-unspecified and closer; ChEBI has no `DL-threonine` term, so that one may need a registry mint rather than a wrong answer.

## 3. Labels have lost their subscripts

Eight ingredient names are unreadable as chemistry because the digits are gone:

| stored label | almost certainly |
|---|---|
| `H BO` | H₃BO₃ boric acid |
| `ZnCl .6H O` | ZnCl₂·6H₂O |
| `Co(NO ) .6H O` | Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O |
| `LiCl.H O` | LiCl·H₂O |
| `As O` | As₂O₃ |
| `Na WO .2H O` | Na₂WO₄·2H₂O |
| `TeO` | TeO₂ |
| `MgSO .7H2O` | MgSO₄·7H₂O |

Note `MgSO .7H2O` keeps the `2` in `H2O` but loses the `4` — so this is not a uniform strip. It looks like subscript characters (₂₃₄) were dropped while ASCII digits survived, which points at an encoding step rather than a parser.

Related typos in the same set, possibly the same origin: `MgSO2·7H2O` (should be SO₄), `NaMoO4·2H2O` ×4 spellings (should be Na₂MoO₄), `Na2Se3 x 5 H2O`, `Na2SeO·5H2O`, `NaSeO3·5H2O`, `Ferric ammmonium citrate`, `Distiled water`.

## Why this matters for #260

Under the agreed direction MIM is the source of truth, so these names need MIM records. But **MIM must not inherit these groundings** — importing them would move the defects rather than fix them, and MIM has no way to tell a good CultureMech id from a bad one without checking each.

So the 44 split roughly:

* ~8 subscript-stripped labels — should be **repaired here**, not recreated in MIM
* ~10 typos and notation variants — likewise
* ~13 genuinely new ingredients MIM should hold, but grounded independently
* the rest are notation variants of substances MIM already has, which become synonyms rather than records

Repairing (1)–(3) here is the higher-value half, because it fixes the source rather than propagating it.
title: Ingredient groundings include a wrong compound, dropped stereochemistry, and subscript-stripped labels
